title: GPU memory budgeting playbook: dynamic split for weights, KV, and activations
creator: Ariana Chen
description:
Purpose: create an operational playbook and runtime estimator that safely budgets GPU memory across three primary consumers: model weights, KV cache, and transient activations under continuous batching. Goal is to avoid OOMs while maximizing utilization and minimizing conservative waste (excess headroom) for production workloads across model families (LLaMA-like, MPT, mix of dense and ALiBi patterns).

Scope: design/implementation of a memory accounting model, an admission control policy for continuous batching, a headroom-margin policy by workload profile, simulated stress tests, and integration points for autoscaler and graceful fallback (weight swap/evict/quantize). This ticket covers the design doc, estimator prototype (offline calculator + lightweight runtime estimator), integration spec for scheduler, and a short experiment run with three representative models and request patterns.

Non-goals: implementing full weight-paged swapping system (separate RFC), long-running distributed KV sharding across GPUs (future ticket), end-user config UI (Console work separate).
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic estimator exists that, given model metadata (size, layer count, per-layer activation multiplier), KV expected growth, and N concurrent in-flight requests distribution, outputs a per-GPU memory allocation plan (weights, KV, activations, headroom) as bytes.
Runtime can reject or route a new request if estimator predicts >95% probability of exceeding safe memory threshold within 200ms of admission decision.
Integration point defined for scheduler to consult estimator for admission decisions and for autoscaler to interpret headroom signals.
Benchmark: in 10K-request simulated trace, OOMs reduced to 0 and average GPU memory waste (reserved but unused) reduced by >=20% vs baseline static 20% headroom policy.
Design doc reviewed and approved by infra and serving runtime leads.
decisions: Use a hybrid accounting model: deterministic lower-bound for weights (resident), probabilistic growth model for KV (workload-driven), and per-request activation estimate derived from peak token length * per-layer multiplier.
Adopt a tiered headroom policy: 10% for steady low-variance workloads; 15-25% for high-variance/PL short-tailed spikes; 30% for unknown/unprofiled workloads until warmed up.
Admission control will consider 'soft reservations' for continuous batching (allow queueing up to soft_limit) and 'hard rejection' when estimated usage > (physical_mem - emergency_margin).

KV eviction first-class option: runtime will evict least-recently-used prefixes when activation budget pressure exceeds threshold, with a configurable minimum KV retention for latency-sensitive sessions.
Weight compression (static per-model quantized artifact) preferred to on-the-fly quantization to avoid CPU/GPU spike; on-the-fly weight quantization remains a fallback with explicit cost accounting.

experiment_summary: We executed a controlled simulation with three workload profiles: (1) low-variance steady traffic (mean request length 32 tokens), (2) mixed traffic with 10% long-tail spikes (up to 1024 tokens), and (3) bursty traffic with inter-arrival time heavy-tail. Baseline: static 20% headroom, no admission control. Our estimator + tiered headroom + KV-eviction strategy achieved: 0 OOMs across traces, 22% less reserved-but-unused memory on average, median tail latency unchanged (<5% difference), and admission decision latency 120ms median. Full logs and aggregated CSVs in attachment bucket.
risks: Estimator underfitting for exotic model architectures (sparse attention variants) — risk mitigated by requiring a short profiling run per new model version before reducing headroom.
KV eviction may increase end-to-end latency for pinned sessions — mitigation: configurable minimum retention and fast multi-level eviction (prefix compression before full eviction).
False positives in admission control could reduce throughput — mitigation: add circuit-breaker that relaxes soft reservation under sustained underutilization for up to 60s.
Operator complexity: more signals for autoscaler and scheduler to ingest — mitigated by providing a small set of normalized signals (estimated_free_bytes, headroom_pct, eviction_pressure).
next_steps: Merge runtime PR for estimator telemetry and admission API (PR 4218) and ensure contracts agreed with scheduler team.
Add a lightweight per-model profiling job to generate activation multipliers and KV-growth priors; store outputs in model metadata catalog.
Implement autoscaler hook to consume estimated_free_bytes and headroom_pct; run canary on staging cluster with 2 GPU nodes.
Add KMS-wrapping for eviction logs and sign-off from security on PII-safe KV eviction metadata.
Schedule a cross-team review (infra, serving, product) for 2026-03-20 to agree rollout plan.
Iterate on estimator: add Bayesian upward-adjustment when rare long sequences observed to reduce one-off OOM risk.
